topicName: Cloud Build: Continuous Integration and Continuous Delivery (CI/CD)
content:
[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Cloud Build: Continuous Integration and Continuous Delivery (CI/CD) on Google Cloud"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"This tutorial provides a comprehensive guide to setting up a CI/CD pipeline using Google Cloud Build. We will cover the essential steps, from configuring your source repository to deploying your application."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Prerequisites"},{"order":4,"type":"bullet_point","text":"A Google Cloud project with billing enabled."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"A source code repository (e.g., GitHub, Cloud Source Repositories, Bitbucket)."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Basic understanding of Docker and containerization."},{"order":7,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 1: Enable the Cloud Build API"},{"order":8,"type":"paragraph","text":"Navigate to the Google Cloud Console and enable the Cloud Build API. Search for 'Cloud Build API' and click 'Enable'."},{"order":9,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 2: Grant Cloud Build Service Account Permissions"},{"order":10,"type":"paragraph","text":"Cloud Build uses a service account to execute builds. You need to grant this service account the necessary permissions to access resources in your project. The default service account is 'PROJECT_NUMBER@cloudbuild.gserviceaccount.com'. Replace PROJECT_NUMBER with your actual project number."},{"order":11,"type":"paragraph","text":"Grant the service account the 'Cloud Build Service Account' role. You might also need to grant other roles depending on your build process (e.g., 'Storage Object Admin' for accessing Cloud Storage buckets, 'App Engine Deployer' for deploying to App Engine)."},{"order":12,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 3: Create a Cloud Build Configuration File (cloudbuild.yaml)"},{"order":13,"type":"paragraph","text":"Create a 'cloudbuild.yaml' file in the root of your repository. This file defines the build steps. Here's a basic example:"},{"order":14,"type":"code","text":"steps:
- name: 'gcr.io/cloud-builders/docker'
  args: ['build', '-t', 'gcr.io/$PROJECT_ID/my-image:$COMMIT_SHA', '.']
- name: 'gcr.io/cloud-builders/docker'
  args: ['push', 'gcr.io/$PROJECT_ID/my-image:$COMMIT_SHA']
- name: 'gcr.io/cloud-builders/kubectl'
  args: ['set', 'image', 'deployment/my-deployment', 'my-container=gcr.io/$PROJECT_ID/my-image:$COMMIT_SHA', '-n', 'my-namespace']
  env: ['CLOUDSDK_COMPUTE_ZONE=us-central1-a', 'CLOUDSDK_CONTAINER_CLUSTER=my-cluster']"},{"order":15,"type":"paragraph","text":"This example builds a Docker image, pushes it to Google Container Registry (GCR), and updates a Kubernetes deployment. Replace 'my-image', 'my-deployment', 'my-container', 'my-namespace', and 'my-cluster' with your actual values."},{"order":16,"type":"paragraph","text":"The '$PROJECT_ID' and '$COMMIT_SHA' are Cloud Build substitution variables that are automatically populated during the build."},{"order":17,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 4: Connect Your Repository to Cloud Build"},{"order":18,"type":"paragraph","text":"In the Google Cloud Console, navigate to Cloud Build -> Triggers. Click 'Create Trigger'."},{"order":19,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Select your source repository (e.g., GitHub, Cloud Source Repositories)."},{"order":20,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Authorize Cloud Build to access your repository."},{"order":21,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Configure the trigger settings:"},{"order":22,"type":"bullet_point","text":"  - **Name:** A descriptive name for your trigger."},{"order":23,"type":"bullet_point","text":"  - **Trigger type:** Choose 'Push to a branch' or 'Push a tag' based on your workflow."},{"order":24,"type":"bullet_point","text":"  - **Branch/Tag:** Specify the branch or tag that will trigger the build (e.g., 'main', 'v*')."},{"order":25,"type":"bullet_point","text":"  - **Build configuration:** Select 'Cloud Build configuration file (yaml or json)' and specify the location of your 'cloudbuild.yaml' file (usually in the root directory)."},{"order":26,"type":"bullet_point","text":"  - **Substitution variables (Optional):** Define any custom substitution variables you need."},{"order":27,"type":"paragraph","text":"Click 'Create' to create the trigger."},{"order":28,"type":"subheading","text":"Step 5: Test Your CI/CD Pipeline"},{"order":29,"type":"paragraph","text":"Make a change to your code and push it to the branch or tag you configured in the trigger. This should automatically trigger a new build in Cloud Build."},{"order":30,"type":"paragraph","text":"Monitor the build progress in the Cloud Build dashboard. Check the logs for any errors."},{"order":31,"type":"subheading","text":"Advanced Configuration"},{"order":32,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Using Service Accounts: For more granular control, create dedicated service accounts for Cloud Build with specific permissions."},{"order":33,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Build Triggers: Configure triggers based on pull requests, tags, or manual invocations."},{"order":34,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Build Steps: Define complex build workflows with multiple steps, including testing, linting, and security scanning."},{"order":35,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Substitution Variables: Use substitution variables to customize your builds based on the trigger event or environment."},{"order":36,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Private Pools: Execute builds in a private pool for enhanced security and isolation."},{"order":37,"type":"subheading","text":"Conclusion"},{"order":38,"type":"paragraph","text":"Cloud Build provides a powerful and flexible platform for implementing CI/CD pipelines on Google Cloud. By following these steps, you can automate your build, test, and deployment processes, improving your development velocity and application quality."}]
